label: build:world
mission: Design a 2.4-3.2 km closed street circuit (pure-math, Node-safe TrackPath + meshes), wet-road shader with planar reflection and analytic streetlight pools, dense procedural downtown (instanced/merged buildings, window atlases, neon signs, billboards, streetlights, traffic lights, overpass), night sky, fog, moonlight shadows, PMREM env map.

structured_report.contract_notes:
- **`startS` is 0.** The start line is at s = 0, about 150 m into the boulevard straight.
  - Grid slots sit at s = L − 9 − 6.5·k (wrapping toward the end of the loop), lateral ∓3.6.
  - Even slots are on the left, so pole is on the outside line for T1 (a right-hander).
  - `getStartGrid` also returns `{ s, lateral }` alongside `position` and `heading`.
- **Track additions (all optional):**
  - `track.setStartLights(n 0..5, go)`: drives the gantry LED start lights. Core does not call it yet; calling it during the countdown would be a nice touch.
  - `getHeadingAt(s)`, which returns a wrapped angle.
  - `project(pos, hintS, out?)`: an optional `out` object avoids allocating per call.
  - Data fields: `lamps` (per-lamp `{ s, kind, color, left, right }`), `lampCount`, `lampGeometry`, `getLampS(k)`.
  - Internals other code may read: `samples`, `corners`, `features` (side streets, junction mouths, crosswalks, kerbs, overpass, `shoreZ` / `isWater`), `grid`, `wet` (shared wet-surface uniforms), `roadMesh`, `barrierMesh`, `reflectionHidden`.
- **Track exports:** `track.js` exports `createTrack`, `createTrackPath` (re-exported from `trackPath.js`) and `lampIntensity`. `createTrackPath()` imports only three and `config.js`, so it works in Node.
- **Environment additions:** `hemiLight`, `sky`, `city`, `lamps`, `signs`, `props`, `reflection`, `fog`, `setRain(0..1)` (puddle ripple and light-cone streak strength), `dispose()`. `createEnvironment` sets `scene.background` and `scene.fog`.
- **Shadow type change:** if the renderer's shadow map type is `PCFSoftShadowMap`, `createEnvironment` switches it to `PCFShadowMap`.
  - three r186 removed PCFSoft and silently falls back on the first shadow render.
  - Without the early switch, programs compiled by the first reflection pass mismatched the shadow sampler and produced GL errors that hid buildings and cars.
  - Core already uses `PCFShadowMap`.
- **Reflection pass:** it does not render on the first frame, only once the main pass has created the moonlight shadow map.
  - When it renders, it draws the whole scene with a mirrored camera, inside `env.update()` and before the main render.
  - Other modules' objects (cars, particles, rain) appear in it automatically, so car and nitro reflections work.
  - Shadow-map updates are disabled during the pass; it copies `camera.layers` and restores the previous render target.
  - Camera-facing sprites from other modules are billboarded toward the virtual camera during that pass.
- **Camera far plane:** the skyline ring reaches 2.65 km, so the camera far plane needs to be at least about 2700. Core uses 3000. The sky dome is pinned to the far plane and follows the camera.
- **Integration:** the environment expects `track` to come from `createTrack`, so the road, ground and water share one reflection. With no `track` it builds only the sky and lights. With no `renderer` it skips the environment map and reflection.
known_issues: Puddle mirrors have fairly crisp edges; when a puddle reflects a large uniform neon glow or the sky's horizon band it can read as a flat coloured patch rather than an image.
Seen from high cameras (intro fly-bys), puddle and water reflections and the plain, unmarked top of the overpass deck look less convincing than at chase height.
The far skyline ring is simple boxed silhouettes with blotchy floor lighting.
Building interiors are flat textures (no interior parallax), and the storefronts repeat recognisably on close inspection.

Streetlights light only the road and sidewalks (computed in the road shader). Buildings and cars get their light from the environment map, moonlight and a street-level glow term, so facades are not lit in pools.
Blade signs use katakana/kanji drawn with system fonts (Hiragino on macOS); on a machine without CJK fonts they would show placeholder boxes.
Steam plumes are not paired with manhole covers in the road paint, and the light cones under streetlights are very subtle.
The hairpin is built as two 90° R26 corners joined by an 18 m straight (a U-turn around a block); the two inner-street legs run parallel about 70 m apart.
GPU timings were taken while other agents were running benches on the same machine, so they are noisy and possibly inflated.
structured_report.perf_notes:
- **Draw calls, bench at chase view (with 5 placeholder cars), each total including the reflection and moonlight-shadow passes:**
  - Boulevard: about 172 per frame, 65 of them in the reflection pass.
  - Overpass: about 113 (40 reflection).
  - Waterfront: about 96 (32 reflection).
  - All are well under the 350 target.
- **Integrated game:** 295–340 draw calls in total with all modules, about 1.9M triangles, 60 fps in headless Chrome at 1280×720 with pixel ratio 1.
- **Static geometry:** about 300k triangles in total:
  - barriers 48k, road ribbon 41k (rows every 4 m on straights, 1 m on curves);
  - lamp poles 31k, waterfront 23k;
  - building tiles about 2k each.
  - Rendered triangles per frame in the bench are about 690k including the reflection and shadow passes.
- **Main levers (each a single draw call):**
  - one shared building material across all tiles;
  - all neon in one additive mesh;
  - instanced lamp poles, lenses, halos and cones, plus instanced signals, beacons, steam and highway traffic;
  - one road shader that does all markings and light pools without extra geometry.
- **GPU time, bench at 1920×1080 with pixel ratio 1 (timer queries):**
  - Reflection pass: about 1.2–2.5 ms.
  - Main scene plus the bench's own bloom: about 8 ms.
  - Road shader: about 2 ms, down from about 4 ms after:
    - moving crosswalk positions into a per-meter texture instead of a 32-step loop;
    - evaluating 2 lamp pairs instead of 3;
    - computing rain ripples only inside nearby puddles.
  - Buildings: about 1 ms.
- **Init time:** about 0.2–1.0 s total across track and environment, mostly procedural textures (facade layers, neon atlas, noise fields).
- **Quality `'low'`:** drops the planar reflection (puddles fall back to the environment map), light cones and steam; uses a 1024 shadow map and lower anisotropy (4 on the asphalt detail texture).
- **Further headroom if needed:** shrink the reflection target (scale 0.4), skip far building tiles in the reflection pass, or drop the light cones.
